# VLY-1

> A tiny deterministic handheld game console designed for AI agents to build complete games on: its own language (VLY),
> a headless toolchain that runs in an agent's sandbox, a test runner with exact hashes, and an optional local MCP server. Cartridges are at most 1 MB, run identically
> in a browser and on hardware, and every run is reproducible.

## Start here (the same steps as https://vly-1.vercel.app/build)

You are asked to make a game for the VLY-1 handheld. Everything you need is one download; building and testing happen on your machine, offline.

1. Download the toolchain (needs Node.js 20+, nothing to install): `curl -sL https://vly-1.vercel.app/vly-cli.tgz | tar xz` makes `./vly`. Then `./vly/bin/vly new mygame` makes an empty project. The step-by-step guide is `https://vly-1.vercel.app/build`.
2. Read the design playbook in full before designing anything: `vly docs design`, or [docs/design.md](docs/design.md); its table of reference guides sends you to the exact recipes for your genre (`vly docs ref-sidescroller` for anything that runs and jumps, `vly docs ref-music` for every game's music; first `vly docs ref-originality` for inventing an idea of your own, `ref-levels` for levels that are fun, `ref-powerups`, `ref-worlds` for structure and exploration). Most bad games here are bad design, not bad code. It covers the quality bar, what the classics teach, familiar-over-clever controls, game feel numbers, readability on 160 x 144, sound, level design and a finishing checklist.
3. The game must be your own: the templates and sample games in `./vly/games/` are references to learn techniques from, never starting points to re-skin. Copy a classic's feel, never its look (Mario's movement is `std/platformer`; bring your own mechanic, theme, sprites and story: `ref-sidescroller` section 0). Write `DESIGN.md` (game in one sentence, controls, screens, a content table, how progress works, a `## Done when` list) and show it to the person before coding.
4. For the front end (splash, menu with CONTINUE first, erase confirmation that defaults to KEEP, how-to page, level grid with locks and grades) copy `vly new mygame --template flow`: the one template meant to be copied. Menus everywhere: UP/DOWN move, A or START choose, B back.
5. Prove it: look at screenshots, record a winning run with a bot, `vly test`, `vly check` clean (it explains any fault: the function, the calls, the variables, a picture and the input to replay). Big data: `bank auto`, and `asset levels bank auto records 240 = incbin("levels.bin")` for many levels (see `vly docs language`).
6. `vly release` does build, tests, check, old-save load, opening recording, publish and verify the link, and an offline copy. Publishing an unlisted play link is optional and needs the person's OK (ask once, up front); the fallback is `vly export build/mygame.vlc --html mygame.html`.

All the docs that matter, as one page: `https://vly-1.vercel.app/llms-full.txt` (build guide, design playbook, language, standard library, modules, two example games). Each doc is also at `https://vly-1.vercel.app/<name>.md` (design, ref-sidescroller, ref-music, workflow, language, stdlib, modules, cli, assembly, distribution, agents, spec, hardware).

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): the fast path for AI agents (workflow, rules of thumb, repo commands)
- [docs/design.md](docs/design.md): the design playbook. Read before designing, and again before calling a game finished
- [docs/ref-sidescroller.md](docs/ref-sidescroller.md): reference guide for running-and-jumping games: the exact Super Mario Bros. movement numbers, collision, camera, level design, and `import "std/platformer"` (a tested module that does it). Read it before building a platformer
- [docs/ref-music.md](docs/ref-music.md): reference guide for music: channel roles, what the classics did, public-domain classical pieces to arrange, loop length, mixing for a tiny speaker. Read it before writing music
- [docs/ref-genres.md](docs/ref-genres.md): reference guide to genres: the recipe, numbers and sample game for a platformer, racer, shooter, puzzle, story, rhythm, virtual pet and versus game. Read the one for your game before you build its core loop.
- [docs/ref-originality.md](docs/ref-originality.md): reference guide to inventing an idea that is yours: a process with random constraints against the first-idea trap, elegance tests, being original in several facets, levels that come from the mechanic. Read it before you choose the game.
- [docs/ref-levels.md](docs/ref-levels.md): reference guide to levels that are fun: every jump needs a consequence, the four beats, pacing, enemy arrangements, terrain; `vly levels` finds dead screens and flat runs.
- [docs/ref-powerups.md](docs/ref-powerups.md): reference guide to power-ups and abilities: why Mario's mushroom and star work, how they really work, a process for inventing your own.
- [docs/ref-readability.md](docs/ref-readability.md): reference guide to seeing what is selected: contrast thresholds, not relying on colour, colour-blind players, four-shade palettes, patterns for highlights, and the `vly highlight`, `vly contrast` and `--cvd` tools.
- [docs/ref-humans.md](docs/ref-humans.md): reference guide to designing for human reaction time, attention and thumbs: reaction versus choice time, latency, frame arithmetic, react-or-anticipate, one decision per beat, forgiveness patterns, bots with reaction delays, a fairness checklist.
- [docs/ref-arcade.md](docs/ref-arcade.md): reference guide to arcade and score-chase games: run structure, fairness by construction, a ladder of bots to measure skill, instant retry, felt events, what brings players back.
- [docs/ref-puzzles.md](docs/ref-puzzles.md): reference guide to puzzle games: a rule that is a picture, a solver and backwards generation, proving every rule bites, par and random-win-rate curves, undo and hints, readability.
- [docs/ref-worlds.md](docs/ref-worlds.md): reference guide to the shape of a game (ten structures beyond the linear scroller), exploring, endings, and atmosphere on a four-colour screen.
- [docs/workflow.md](docs/workflow.md): the build/run/test loop in detail, recorded bots, releases
- [docs/language.md](docs/language.md): the VLY language, including banks (`bank auto`, `records`)
- [docs/stdlib.md](docs/stdlib.md): standard library reference
- [docs/modules.md](docs/modules.md): std/flow (menu, erase confirmation, grades, level grid, buttons), std/ui (menus, dialogue), std/anim, std/music (a three-voice tracker), and ASCII level maps

## Reference

- [docs/distribution.md](docs/distribution.md): exporting one-file games, the native player, WebAssembly, npm
- [docs/cli.md](docs/cli.md): the `vly` command line tool, input scripts, test specs, JSON output
- [docs/assembly.md](docs/assembly.md): assembly language and directives
- [SPEC.md](SPEC.md): the console specification (CPU, memory map, video, input, save, audio, conformance)
- [CONTRACTS.md](CONTRACTS.md): on-chain design (chunks, game contract, saves)
- [docs/hardware.md](docs/hardware.md): the hardware plan: HAL, device loop, RP2040 port, pinout, display options, BOM, what is proven and what is not
- [hardware/](hardware/): hal.h, device.c, host test, RP2040 firmware, vlc2c.js, bom.csv
- [spec/isa.json](spec/isa.json): the instruction set as data; [spec/font.json](spec/font.json): the built-in font

## Tools

- `node cli/vly.js` (or `vly`): build, run, test, tiles, docs, chunks, mcp
- `vly mcp`: Model Context Protocol server with vly_build, vly_run (returns screenshots), vly_test, vly_tiles, vly_docs
- [templates/](templates/): techniques to learn from (hello, game, pong, battle, platformer, puzzle, shooter); `flow` is the one meant to be copied (menu, save, grades, level grid)
